title: MongoDB
description: MongoDB processes -- standalone mongod, replica set members, and the shard members, config servers and mongos routers of a sharded cluster -- as collected by the startechnica/grafana mongodb_metrics module. Panels select by metric name, so a MongoDB scraped by a separate mongodb_exporter in compatible mode shows up too. Replica sets are told apart by name (and cluster_name when it is set).

list.name: cluster
list.label: Cluster
list.description: The cluster_name label, when the collectors set one.

panels.title: Processes up
panels.description: MongoDB processes (mongod and mongos) the exporter can connect and authenticate to.

panels.title: Processes down
panels.description: Processes the exporter cannot reach or authenticate to: down, not accepting connections, or rejecting the monitoring user (a shard member of a sharded cluster needs a shard-local one).

panels.title: Replica sets without a primary
panels.description: Replica sets in which no reporting member sees a PRIMARY. Writes to them fail.

targets.expr: count(max by (cluster_name, rs_nm) (mongodb_rs_members_state{cluster_name=~"$cluster"} == bool 1) == 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Unreachable members
panels.description: Replica set members that some other member cannot heartbeat.

targets.expr: count(min by (cluster_name, rs_nm, member_idx) (mongodb_rs_members_health{cluster_name=~"$cluster"}) == 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Worst replication lag
panels.description: The furthest any secondary is behind its primary.

panels.title: Shortest oplog window
panels.description: The least time any selected member's oplog spans. A member away for longer than its window has to resync all of its data.

panels.title: Processes
panels.description: One row per MongoDB process. Type is what the exporter found (mongod or mongos); Role and Replica set come from the process itself (shardsvr, configsvr, or empty for a plain replica set). Connections used is against the process's connection limit.

targets.expr: max by (instance) (mongodb_connections{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}", state="current"} / ignoring (state) (mongodb_connections{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}", state="current"} + ignoring (state) mongodb_connections{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}", state="available"}))

panels.title: Member state
panels.description: Each replica set member's own state over time. PRIMARY changing hands is an election; a gap means the member was not scraped or its exporter could not connect.

panels.title: Replication lag
panels.description: Seconds each secondary is behind its primary, from the members' own replica set status. Members are named as in the replica set configuration.

panels.title: Oplog window
panels.description: How much time each member's oplog spans: how long a member can be away and still catch up from it. The dashed lines are 1 hour and 1 day.

panels.title: Replicated operations applied
panels.description: Operations a secondary applies from its primary's oplog, per second.

panels.title: Operations by type
panels.description: Operations per second across the selected processes, by type. Commands include the replica set's and the sharding layer's own traffic.

panels.title: Operations by process
panels.description: Operations per second on each process, all types together.

panels.title: Average latency
panels.description: Average time an operation spends in mongod, by kind, over the last rate interval; a kind with no operations in it is left out.

panels.title: Documents per second
panels.description: Documents returned, inserted, updated and deleted per second across the selected processes.

panels.title: Documents scanned per document returned
panels.description: Documents the queries examined for each one they returned. Close to 1 means the indexes fit the queries; far above it means collection scans or poor indexes.

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (rate(mongodb_mongod_metrics_query_executor_total{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}", state="scanned_objects"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (instance) (rate(mongodb_mongod_metrics_document_total{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}", state="returned"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Asserts
panels.description: Asserts per second, by type, where there are any. Regular asserts are server errors; user asserts are the clients' (bad queries, duplicate keys).

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Client connections open on each process.

panels.title: Tickets in use
panels.description: WiredTiger read and write tickets in use. When all are in use, further operations queue.

panels.title: Queued operations
panels.description: Operations waiting for a lock, by readers and writers.

panels.title: Open cursors
panels.description: Cursors open on each process. A count that only grows points at clients that do not close theirs.

panels.title: Transactions
panels.description: Multi-document transactions committed and aborted per second.

panels.title: WiredTiger cache
panels.description: Cache fill and dirty data as a share of the configured cache. The dashed lines are where WiredTiger makes application threads evict pages themselves: 20% dirty, 95% full.

panels.title: Cache evictions
panels.description: Pages evicted from the WiredTiger cache per second. Modified pages have to be written first.

panels.title: Resident memory
panels.description: Memory each mongod or mongos holds in RAM.

panels.title: Page faults
panels.description: Page faults per second: reads the operating system had to satisfy from disk.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Bytes per second received and sent by each process.

panels.title: Databases
panels.description: Per database, as each replica set reports it, and as mongos reports it for the whole sharded cluster (Role mongos). Storage size is what the data takes on disk after compression.

targets.expr: max by (cluster_name, cl_role, rs_nm, database) (mongodb_dbstats_dataSize{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}"})
max by (cluster_name, cl_role, rs_nm, database) (mongodb_dbstats_storageSize{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}"})
max by (cluster_name, cl_role, rs_nm, database) (mongodb_dbstats_indexSize{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}"})
max by (cluster_name, cl_role, rs_nm, database) (mongodb_dbstats_objects{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}"})
max by (cluster_name, cl_role, rs_nm, database) (mongodb_dbstats_collections{cluster_name=~"$cluster", instance=~"${instance:regex}"})

panels.title: Shards
panels.description: Shards in the cluster, as mongos reports it.

panels.title: Chunks
panels.description: Chunks across all sharded collections.

panels.title: Sharded collections
panels.description: Collections that are sharded.

panels.title: Balancer
panels.description: Whether the balancer is enabled. Backups and maintenance turn it off on purpose.

panels.title: Balancer activity
panels.description: Whether the balancer is moving chunks right now.

panels.title: Draining shards
panels.description: Shards being removed, whose chunks the balancer is moving away.

panels.title: Chunks per shard
panels.description: Chunks each shard owns. The balancer moves chunks to even these out.
